name: Prompt Repetition
executive_summary: Simply duplicate the entire prompt back-to-back so left-to-right attention can reach information that only appeared later — improving accuracy on non-reasoning tasks for most models with no added output length.
description: Addresses the same causal-masking root cause as Lost in the Middle and Found-in-the-Middle Calibration, but with the simplest possible mitigation: standard decoder-only LLMs process text left-to-right, so a token early in the prompt (e.g. answer options listed before the passage they refer to) cannot attend to content that appears after it in a single pass. Repeating the full prompt verbatim means every token's second occurrence can now attend to the entire first occurrence, approximating bidirectional attention without any architecture change. Tested across 7 models (Gemini 2.0 Flash/Flash Lite, GPT-4o/4o-mini, Claude 3 Haiku/3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek V3) and 7 benchmarks (ARC-Challenge, OpenBookQA, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, MATH, plus two custom positional-sensitivity benchmarks) on non-reasoning generation: repetition won 47/70 model-benchmark combinations with 0 losses (statistically significant by McNemar's test), including gains up to 76% on some retrieval/lookup tasks, with no increase in output length and no added latency for most models tested — the paper notes Anthropic's Claude models as the exception to the latency-neutrality claim. In reasoning-enabled mode the benefit is much smaller (reported as 5 wins vs. 22 ties in that setting), consistent with the paper's own observation that RL-trained reasoning models often already learn to repeat parts of the request on their own.
when_to_use: Non-reasoning generation (direct answers, classification, retrieval/lookup from a provided passage, multiple-choice) where cost and latency matter and a free, single-call formatting change is preferred over more expensive techniques.
Cases resembling 'Lost in the Middle' symptoms — answer options or instructions appearing before the content they depend on.
when_not_to_use: Reasoning-enabled generation (explicit chain-of-thought or 'thinking' modes) — reported benefit there was much weaker (5 wins vs. 22 ties across the same test matrix), consistent with reasoning models often already exhibiting similar re-reading behavior on their own.
Tasks where doubling the input token count meaningfully affects cost under a strict prompt-token budget, even though output length is unaffected.

Deployments on Claude models specifically where added latency from the longer input hasn't been separately verified — the paper notes Claude as the exception to its general latency-neutrality finding.
known_pitfalls: The underlying experiments were run against model versions current as of early-to-mid 2025 (Gemini 2.0, GPT-4o family, Claude 3.x, DeepSeek V3) — later model generations released since are untested, so the specific magnitude of reported gains (up to 76% on some tasks) should be treated as demonstrated on that model generation, not guaranteed to hold identically on newer ones, even though the underlying causal-masking mechanism the technique addresses is architecture-level and plausibly still applies.
The 'no added latency' finding has a noted exception for Anthropic's Claude models specifically — verify latency impact empirically before assuming it's free on every provider.

This is a December 2025 preprint, not yet peer-reviewed at time of cataloging — the experimental design (7 models, 70 combinations, McNemar significance testing) is solid, but independent replication by other labs hadn't been found as of this entry's most recent check.

variables.name: original_prompt
variables.description: The complete original prompt (instructions, context, question), repeated verbatim immediately after itself with no separator needed

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
